threads.body: `__copy__` returning `copy(self.__wrapped__)` will generally drop the tracing wrapper (and, depending on what `__wrapped__` is, may return an uninstrumented callable). This undermines the goal of copying *wrapped* DSPy methods while keeping behavior consistent (including emitting spans). Instead, `__copy__` should return a new `_CopyableBoundFunctionWrapper` (or even `self`) that retains `_self_wrapper`/`_self_enabled` and binding; and `__deepcopy__` should similarly return a bound wrapper tied to the deep-copied instance, without falling back to `copy(self)` (which currently routes through the problematic `__copy__` path).

 _REACT_V2_CLASS = "ReActV2"
 
 
+class _CopyableBoundFunctionWrapper(BoundFunctionWrapper[Any, Any]):
+    """BoundFunctionWrapper that supports copy and deepcopy."""
+
+    def __copy__(self) -> Any:
+        wrapped: Any = self.__wrapped__
+        return copy(wrapped)
+
+    def __deepcopy__(self, memo: dict[Any, Any]) -> Any:
+        if self._self_instance is not None:
+            copied_instance: Any = deepcopy(self._self_instance, memo)
+            attr_name: str | None = getattr(self, "__name__", None)
+            if attr_name and hasattr(copied_instance, attr_name):
+                return getattr(copied_instance, attr_name)
+        return copy(self)

threads.body: `wrap_object()` expects an actual module/object as `target` and an attribute name (typically not a dotted path). In this patch, callers pass `tool_module` / `_REACT_MODULE` (module name strings) and names like `"Tool.__call__"` / `"ReAct.forward"`, which likely breaks patching at runtime (e.g., `AttributeError` on a `str`, or failure to resolve dotted attributes). Consider implementing `_wrap_function` to (1) import the module when given a string, (2) resolve dotted attribute paths to the owner object + final attribute, and (3) `getattr`/`setattr` the wrapped attribute using `_CopyableFunctionWrapper`. This preserves the previous `wrap_function_wrapper` behavior while enabling the custom wrapper class.

 _REACT_V2_CLASS = "ReActV2"
 
 
+class _CopyableBoundFunctionWrapper(BoundFunctionWrapper[Any, Any]):
+    """BoundFunctionWrapper that supports copy and deepcopy."""
+
+    def __copy__(self) -> Any:
+        wrapped: Any = self.__wrapped__
+        return copy(wrapped)
+
+    def __deepcopy__(self, memo: dict[Any, Any]) -> Any:
+        if self._self_instance is not None:
+            copied_instance: Any = deepcopy(self._self_instance, memo)
+            attr_name: str | None = getattr(self, "__name__", None)
+            if attr_name and hasattr(copied_instance, attr_name):
+                return getattr(copied_instance, attr_name)
+        return copy(self)
+
+
+class _CopyableFunctionWrapper(FunctionWrapper[Any, Any]):
+    """FunctionWrapper that supports copy and deepcopy."""
+
+    __bound_function_wrapper__ = _CopyableBoundFunctionWrapper
+
+    def __copy__(self) -> _CopyableFunctionWrapper:
+        wrapped: Any = self.__wrapped__
+        wrapper: Any = self._self_wrapper
+        return _CopyableFunctionWrapper(
+            copy(wrapped),
+            wrapper,
+            self._self_enabled,
+        )
+
+    def __deepcopy__(self, memo: dict[Any, Any]) -> _CopyableFunctionWrapper:
+        wrapped: Any = self.__wrapped__
+        wrapper: Any = self._self_wrapper
+        return _CopyableFunctionWrapper(
+            deepcopy(wrapped, memo),
+            wrapper,
+            self._self_enabled,
+        )
+
+
+def _wrap_function(
+    target: Any,
+    name: str,
+    wrapper: Callable[..., Any],
+) -> None:
+    wrap_object(target, name, _CopyableFunctionWrapper, (wrapper,))

threads.body: The `if hasattr(tool, "acall"):` block is redundant because the test is already guarded by `@pytest.mark.skipif(not hasattr(dspy.Tool, "acall"), ...)`. Keeping the runtime branch makes the test easier to accidentally “pass” without asserting anything (if conditions ever diverge), and adds unnecessary indentation. Suggest removing the `if` and unindenting the assertions; also the inner `import dspy` is redundant since the module already imports `dspy` at the top for the skipif condition.

The `owner` argument requires wrapt >= 1.17, but the package declares no wrapt bound and gets `wrapt >= 1.0.0` transitively from `opentelemetry-instrumentation`. On 1.14/1.15/1.16 every copy raises:

```
TypeError: FunctionWrapperBase() takes at most 6 arguments (7 given)
```

add `wrapt >= 1.17` to `dependencies` (portkey already declares wrapt). The `oldest` env won't catch this - wrapt is transitive, so `lowest-direct` still resolves the newest.

The tests only copy a bound method directly, which is not what DSPy does. The case that actually breaks today is a module tree holding an instrumented bound method - e.g. the agent-as-tool pattern:

```python
sub = dspy.ReAct("question -> answer", tools=[...])
tool = dspy.Tool(func=sub.forward, name="subagent", desc="d")
outer = dspy.ReAct("question -> answer", tools=[tool])
copy.deepcopy(outer)   # NotImplementedError without this PR
```

Worth covering that instead of / in addition to the direct-copy cases, and asserting the copied module still emits spans when called (right now the ReAct copies are only checked for `is not None`).

Also the `try/except (ImportError, AttributeError): pass` around ReActV2 means that block silently asserts nothing on versions where it does exist and something else goes wrong - a `pytest.importorskip` would fail loudly instead.
